result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.node_percolation()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Simulate node percolation by randomly removing nodes. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L14954-L15006){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.node_percolation( q, seed=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Percolation](/assets/graphs/algo-percolation.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="On the left, a connected six-node graph laid out in two rows of three. On the right, the two middle-column nodes and every edge incident to them are shown as faded dashed ghost outlines, indicating that they have been removed. The four remaining nodes have split into two disconnected pairs." width="100%"} Creates a new graph with a fraction of nodes randomly removed, along with all their incident edges. This is useful for analyzing network robustness under random node failures. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [q]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Fraction of nodes to remove (must be between `0.0` and `1.0`). For example, `q=0.2` removes 20% of nodes. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Random seed for reproducibility. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A new Graph containing only the surviving nodes and edges. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Remove 30% of nodes randomly: ::: {#4d63deda .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph(directed=False) graph.add_full_graph(10) # Remove 30% of nodes randomly percolated = graph.node_percolation(q=0.3, seed=23) # Returns 7 - number of nodes remaining after percolation percolated.count_nodes() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 7 ``` ::: :::
